nodes.description: Systemic LASV infection of endothelium and mononuclear phagocytes disrupts endothelial regulation of hemostasis, platelet activity, complement, and inflammatory mediators. The resulting capillary dilation and increased vascular permeability cause facial swelling, serosal effusions, hypotension, shock, and multi-organ failure in severe Lassa fever.

nodes.description: LASV glycoprotein first binds matriglycan on α-dystroglycan at the cell surface, is internalized by endocytosis, then switches in the acidifying endosome to LAMP1 binding so the viral membrane can fuse and release the ambisense RNA genome into the cytosol.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of residues in Lassa virus glycoprotein 1 involved in receptor switch.
